title: Mapping the nanoscale organization of the human cell surface proteome reveals new functional associations and surface antigen clusters.
authors: Floyd, Brendan M; Schmidt, Elizabeth L; Till, Nicholas A; Yang, Jonathan L; Liao, Pinyu; George, Benson M; Flynn, Ryan A; Bertozzi, Carolyn R
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文通过邻近标记和质谱绘制细胞表面蛋白质组空间图谱，虽涉及转录因子TFAM的表面定位，但核心是表面蛋白组织而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: The cell surface is a dynamic interface that controls cell-cell communication and signal transduction relevant to organ development, homeostasis and repair, immune reactivity, and pathologies driven by aberrant cell surface phenotypes. The spatial organization of cell surface proteins is central to these processes. High-resolution fluorescence microscopy and proximity labeling have advanced studies of surface protein associations, but the spatial organization of the complete surface proteome remains uncharted. In this study, we systematically mapped the surface proteome of human T-lymphocytes and B-lymphoblasts using proximity labeling of 85 antigens, identified from over 100 antibodies tested for binding to surface-exposed proteins. These experiments were coupled with an optimized data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry workflow to generate a robust dataset. Unsupervised clustering of the resulting interactome revealed functional modules, including well-characterized complexes such as the T-cell receptor and HLA class I/II, alongside novel clusters. Notably, we identified mitochondrial proteins localized to the surface, including the transcription factor TFAM, suggesting previously unappreciated roles for mitochondrial proteins at the plasma membrane. A high-accuracy machine learning classifier predicted over 6,000 surface protein associations, highlighting functional associations such as IL10RB's role as a negative regulator of type I interferon signaling. Spatial modeling of the surface proteome provided insights into protein dispersion patterns, distinguishing widely distributed proteins, such as CD45, from localized antigens, such as CD226 pointing to active mechanisms of regulating surface organization. This work provides a comprehensive map of the human surfaceome and a resource for exploring the spatial and functional dynamics of the cell membrane proteome.
abstract_zh: 细胞表面是一个动态界面，控制着与器官发育、稳态与修复、免疫反应以及由异常细胞表面表型驱动的病理过程相关的细胞间通讯和信号转导。细胞表面蛋白的空间组织对这些过程至关重要。高分辨率荧光显微镜和邻近标记技术推进了表面蛋白关联的研究，但完整表面蛋白质组的空间组织仍未被绘制。在本研究中，我们通过85种抗原的邻近标记，系统性地绘制了人类T淋巴细胞和B淋巴母细胞的表面蛋白质组，这些抗原是从100多种经测试与表面暴露蛋白结合的抗体中鉴定出来的。这些实验与优化的数据非依赖采集质谱工作流程相结合，生成了一个稳健的数据集。对所得相互作用组的无监督聚类揭示了功能模块，包括如T细胞受体和HLA I/II类等特征明确的复合物，以及新发现的聚类。值得注意的是，我们鉴定了定位于表面的线粒体蛋白，包括转录因子TFAM，提示线粒体蛋白在质膜上可能具有此前未被认识的作用。一个高精度的机器学习分类器预测了超过6,000种表面蛋白关联，突出了功能关联，如IL10RB作为I型干扰素信号负调控因子的作用。表面蛋白质组的空间建模提供了对蛋白分布模式的见解，区分了如CD45等广泛分布的蛋白与如CD226等局部化抗原，指向调控表面组织的活性机制。这项工作提供了人类表面组（surfaceome）的全面图谱，以及探索细胞膜蛋白质组空间和功能动态的资源。
